trial_court: Sessions Judge, Kurnool, Sessions Case No.63 of 2018
case_name: B. Parvathi vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh
facts_of_case: Accused Nos.1 and 2 were charged with various IPC sections for the death of Vishali. Accused No.1 was accused of marrying Vishali knowing she had a heart ailment. Accused No.2 was accused of harassing Vishali to accept her husband's second marriage.

legal_principles.principle: The Judge is not a mere post office to frame the charge at the behest of the prosecution, but has to exercise his judicial mind to determine whether a case for trial has been made out by the prosecution.
legal_principles.held: If, upon consideration of the record of the case and the documents submitted therewith, and after hearing the submissions of the accused and the prosecution in this behalf, the Judge considers that there is not sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused, he shall discharge the accused and record his reasons for so doing.
cited_cases: Union of India v. Prafulla Kumar Samal

legal_principles.principle: The Judge has the undoubted power to sift and weigh the evidence for the limited purpose of finding out whether or not a prima facie case against the accused has been made out.
legal_principles.held: The test to determine prima facie case would depend upon the facts of each case.

outcome.final_order: The petition filed under Section 227 Cr.P.C. by the petitioner to discharge her from the case was dismissed.

keywords: Latin Maxim: Nemo judex in causa sua
